raw_recipe.headline: Poppyseed Salad Dressing
raw_recipe.description: Freshly made onion juice is the family secret to this old recipe for a sweet and tangy poppyseed salad dressing that's ready in just a few minutes.
raw_recipe.name: Poppyseed Salad Dressing

recipeInstructions.text: In a 1-quart jar with a lid, mix together the sugar, mustard powder, vegetable oil, poppy seeds, salt, white vinegar, and onion juice; tighten the lid onto the jar, and shake vigorously to combine. Reshake the dressing before using.

review.reviewBody: Hi Everyone - This is my recipe. Onion juice can be found at most grocery stores. You can find it in the spice aisle. DO NOT USE immitation onion juice - it makes a difference. (I've never tried making my own onion juice, but I'll look forward to others that try it and post results - see editor's note.) This recipe makes a lot of dressing. You can refrigerate the left-over dressing for a long time to have on-hand. Enjoy!

I substituted Splenda for the sugar to make the recipe more diabetic friendly, but otherwise used the ingredients as stated, though I made just one-fourth of the recipe to try it out. I did, however, change the technique. I added all ingredients except the oil and the poppy seeds to the bowl of a food processor and mixed. Then I added the oil gradually through the top of the processor bowl with the motor running. The dressing emulsified well this way. I added the poppy seeds at the end and just pulsed a few times.

This was a tasty dressing which I used today over mixed greens. Tomorrow I plan to add a few kiwi slices and mandarin oranges with the greens and use this dressing again. Next time I make the dressing, I'll probably use a bit less sweetener, as it seems just a little sweeter than I prefer, but as a diabetic I'm used to things less sweet.

We use Poppyseed Dressing most of the time so I thought I would try making it myself and this recipe was so easy and delicious I should never have to buy it ready made again. Following the instructions from another review I grated part of an onion (I used a sweet onion) and pressed it through a small sieve to make the onion juice, it couldn't be easier! Added all the ingredients into my blender and in a couple minutes it was blended perfectly and ready to go. Thanks for a delicious recipe!

Couldn't find onion juice so I used my microplane which grated the onion into a fine, watery "baby food" consistency. It blended perfectly into the dressing. My husband and I agree, this dressing is better than the one our favorite restaurant makes.

WOW..very good dressing, I used a Blendtec blender on the dressing button to make this dressing, and pulsed in the poppy seeds at the end and it came out perfectly emulsified and creamy..I used 1/2 Sugar and 1/2 Splenda..I used it for a slaw recipe of cabbage, carrots and raisins...I can't wait to try on a spinach salad..yum...also followed editors note and made my own onion juice (I pureed 1/2 a med onion in a mini chopper and pressed thru a fine strainer)
It was very tasty! Couldn't find onion juice at the grocery store, so puréed a small onion in a mini food processor and squeezed purée through a small sieve.

Turned out just great!! I coudn't find opinion and mustard powder so I put in fresh onions and mustard seeds instead and blended them in the magic bullet first; it worked really well. Definite crowd pleaser...thanks so much :)

Great taste. I couldn't find onion juice and substitued onion powder instead. Probably not as good, but still very tasty. I did find it a bit sweet when it was done so I added the juice of a fresh lemon which added to the flavor and cut the sweetness.

This is an AMAZING recipe! Everyone who tries it,loves it. I even gave it in fancy little jars for Christmas gifts. Thanks so much. 
 I use it on a spinach salad with candied pecans (or candied bacon), goat cheese. blueberries and red onion.
This was waayyyy too sweet! I'd cut the sugar in half to start! After I doubled the other ingredients & added some apple cider vinegar, it was tolerable.

I am on the Ideal Protein diet and don't like any of the other "diet" salad dressings. I adjusted the servings to one, then substituted 1 pkt Splenda for sugar, sea salt for salt, olive oil instead of vegetable oil and just slightly less vinegar. It is delicious, I drizzled it on grilled chicken and zucchini. I'll be using this all the time.
I thought this was delicious. The hardest part was grating the onion, and it really wasn't hard at all! I made 1/3 of the recipe since there is only 2 of us. Thanks for sharing your recipe.
I usually purchase poppy seed dressing but not any more! This dressing was great.
Not great, tasted too much like oil :(

Alley, I've made this more times than I can remember & my family continues to still ask for it. I had an old copy from 2013 & needed to reprint; had a difficult time finding it on Allrecipes; found it when I googled, thank goodness because my copy was too worn to copy for anyone else. I will say this to everyone......the onion juice does make the difference. Chop your onion extra fine then squeeze it through cheesecloth! Believe me it's worth the effort. Enjoy! Loviedove
I have made this at least 10 times and it is consistently well received. While it is too sweet to serve all the time, it is a staple in our house.

I saw this recipe a few years ago in a magazine and loved it. Went to look for it recently to no avail. Thank goodness it was in Allrecipes. It is an excellent dressing. If you change the recipe then you cannot ''rate''it as it is y ours and not as on this site. It is a light sweet recipe perfect for a spinach salad with fresh strawberries; on a grilled chicken wrap; wherever you like. Lovely. Thanks for sharing.
I didn't have onion juice, so ran some diced onion through the food processor. Turned out great!

I find this dressing too oily in consistency for me. I prefer the poppyseed dressing made with mayo. These dressings pack a lot of calories, so I'm going to try making the mayo variety with unsweetened Greek yogurt next time.
It's now a staple in my kitchen. We don't buy store-packaged salad dressings anymore.
